text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Wednesday.
- U.N. has bought 7,700 weapons from the local population in Croatia's last Serb-held enclave, with the money secured by the Croatian government.
- We can allow only three-month extension of the U.N. mandate in Eastern Slavonia, plus another three months for withdrawal of the U.N. troops, says President Franjo Tudjman.

- Director of the Paris-based Simon Wiesenthal Centre Shimon Samuels apologised to Croatian Post after mistakenly accusing it of issuing a stamp honouring a war criminal, when the stamp in fact only carried a name of its designer, the criminal's namesake.
- American Bell helicopters that Defence Ministry plans to buy from the U.S. will open the door for Croatia's admission into Partnership for Peace.

- Opposition parties in the upper house of parliament have challenged the recently passed denationalisation law before the Constitutional court, saying some of its provisions violate the constitution.

- Croatia and Yugoslavia will sign ten agreements on issues relating to the normalisation proces by the end of this year. Croatian Foreign Minister and his Yugoslav counterpart agreed in Zagreb on Tuesday to scrap visas for diplomats.
- Croatian foreign service will cost 280 million kuna this year, or some 0.8 percent of the state budget.
- Croatia's external debt has risen to $4.5 bln from $2.6 billion in the past three years. Most foreign borrowing still consumption and not investment oriented.
- Davor Juric, head of the association of independent trade unions, announces tough talks with employers on pay rises.
- Money market: Overnight liquidity of the banking sector has improved but demand for term loans is on the increase, boosting lending rates.
- Shipper Croatia Line opens its third foreign representative office in Milan, Italy. The company had a profit of $852,000 in 1995 on a total income of $261 million.
- Following the collapse of the Banca di Credito di Trieste the fate of Croatian deposits totalling more than 100 billion lira is still uncertain.

-- Average net salary in September totalled 2,085 kuna (581 German marks), 0.7 percent up from August and 13.4 percent up from the same month last year. With 3,020 kuna insurers had the highest August salary.
- Central bank says it will reform the payments system soon.
- Capital market: shares of Zagrebacka Banka and drugs firm Pliva proved the most lucrative investment in the first nine months of 1996. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
